purpose: Resolve the pre-contact observation-network data gate without inventing a false exact count across unlike radar, DF/ESM, air-reconnaissance, visual-watch and plotting assets.
adjudication_rule: R-SCIENCE-COMPARE-LIKE / bounded-not-absent: heterogeneous sensor/reporting assets are not collapsed into one physical station count.

accounting_decision.reason: The prior open node mixed physical radar sites, radio/DF collection, reconnaissance detachments, coastal visual observation and plot/reporting cells. These have different definitions and readiness clocks.
accounting_decision.replacement: Count functional reporting nodes by role/readiness and keep physical radar-site count separately UNKNOWN unless dated source evidence identifies installations.

physical_radar_station_count.note: Later 1944 evidence confirms plural Japanese radar installations in the Andamans, but it does not justify back-dating an exact 1 Jan count.

source_anchors.supports: Akyab/Port Blair active sensor layer; Ceylon/Addu passive observation logic.
Chittagong/Patenga damaged but partially restored year-end air/recon capacity; 15-25 regular fighter/recon presence band.
Japanese low/mid-grade COMINT and passive ESM may cue search sectors but do not create automatic weapon-quality tracks.

source_anchors.title: Japanese Air Raid on Calcutta – December 1943
source_anchors.supports: 331 Air Group detachments reported at Mergui and Port Blair; 705 Air Group sea-search activity from Padang/Sabang.

source_anchors.title: Contribution of RN aircraft carriers (King's College thesis)
source_anchors.supports: June 1944 Illustrious strike at Port Blair included two radar stations; proves plural radar installations by mid-1944 only, not exact Jan count.

source_anchors.title: History of Electronic Warfare / Congressional Record extract
source_anchors.supports: Australian/British ferret aircraft from India plotted Japanese radars on the Andaman Islands and Malay Peninsula during the war.

functional_forward_nodes.historical_or_branch_basis: Established Japanese-side Bay/Arakan sensor base in Branch planning; not newly captured.
Established Andaman base with air detachment/traffic; later 1944 evidence proves multiple radar stations, exact Jan count unresolved.
Mergui outlying fighter/air presence corroborated; treat Victoria Point as sector support, not a separately proven radar station.
Captured 15 Dec; heavy demolition and repair debt. Branch year-end allows regular 15-25 fighter/recon presence, so useful but not mature/dense sensor coverage.

rear_support_nodes.note: Rear search support; not counted as Andaman-Arakan forward physical station.
Reporting/liaison node, not direct wide-area visual/radar coverage.

countable_summary.ready_equivalent_method: HIGH=1.0, MEDIUM_HIGH=0.85, MEDIUM=0.7 used only as planning coverage diagnostic; not a combat multiplier.

contact_quality_rule.cue_level: Any one node may create bearing/sector/time-window cue.
contact_quality_rule.track_level: Requires repeated reports or a second modality/node to narrow track age/route.
contact_quality_rule.weapon_quality: Requires fresh air/seaplane/submarine/visual recontact. Passive ESM/DF or a single radar/visual report never grants automatic firing solution.
contact_quality_rule.do_not_double_count: Air-recon detachment and its report relay at the same node are one causal chain, not two independent detection bonuses.

open_after_this_audit: Exact Jan-1944 hardware inventory/radar-set count at each node remains source-unknown and is not required to proceed with the first indication gate.
Weather, sortie availability and contact freshness are event-time variables and must be resolved when the RN force actually enters local search geometry.
